subject: Catalyst integration incident — support coordination and SLA runbook
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@catalystsys.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: partner-support@catalystsys.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: connector errors in production (Catalyst <-> Redwood)

Hi Mateo / Camila —

We started seeing a spike in 500s from the Redwood connector at ~15:40 PDT this afternoon. Impact: our enrichment pipeline backs up and downstream model scoring is delayed ~25–40 minutes. We retried a few requests and saw intermittent success, then consistent failures.

Attached is a short error dump and a sample request/response (headers only) to help triage. We need this escalated — our SLO is 99.9% for the enrichment task and this pushes us over the daily threshold. Can you confirm you have someone on this and an ETA for a patch or mitigation?

Logs attached: catalyst-error-log-20260711.txt (zipped excerpt)

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Catalyst Solutions, Inc.

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@catalystsys.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, partner-support@catalystsys.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: connector errors in production (Catalyst <-> Redwood)

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick flag. I’ve looped in Jonas (platform on-call) and Camila from Partnerships so we can coordinate directly with Catalyst.

Immediate plan:
- Jonas will triage the serving logs and confirm whether this is a model-side 500 or a routing/proxy issue.
- If it’s a transient routing fault we can re-route traffic to the warm pool within 10–15 minutes.
- Please share any additional request ids or sample payloads — the headers file you attached was helpful; more samples speed root cause.

Jonas: can you take first pass and post findings here? If we need to escalate to infra we’ll open RED-3245 and CC infra on the ticket.

Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Partnerships Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, Alex Chen <alex.chen@catalystsys.com>
Cc: partner-support@catalystsys.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: connector errors in production (Catalyst <-> Redwood)

Thanks — I pulled the request ids Alex provided and matched them to our proxy logs. Initial notes:
- Between 15:37–15:52 PDT we observed elevated 502/504 at the edge for that routing shard; backend LLM nodes returned valid responses in ~60% of retries.
- There is a partial KV cache miss pattern consistent with recent kernel rollout on that pool (we did a behind-the-scenes patch earlier today).
- Mitigation: I’ve kicked a temporary routing rule to avoid the updated pool for Catalyst’s org-id. That will route to the stable warm pool; expected effect: reduced latency + fewer 5xxs.

I attached a short sample of the headers I inspected: initial-sample-headers.txt.

Immediate ask for Catalyst: please confirm you can resume traffic test now (we’ll watch for error rate to drop below 0.1%). If it doesn’t, we’ll open RED-3245 and escalate to infra and SRE.

On-call — Jonas Weber
Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@catalystsys.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, partner-support@catalystsys.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: connector errors in production (Catalyst <-> Redwood)

On Sat, Jul 11, 2026 at 5:02 PM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — I pulled the request ids Alex provided and matched them to our proxy logs. Initial notes:
> - Between 15:37–15:52 PDT we observed elevated 502/504 at the edge for that routing shard; backend LLM nodes returned valid responses in ~60% of retries.
> - There is a partial KV cache miss pattern consistent with recent kernel rollout on that pool (we did a behind-the-scenes patch earlier today).
> - Mitigation: I’ve kicked a temporary routing rule to avoid the updated pool for Catalyst’s org-id. That will route to the stable warm pool; expected effect: reduced latency + fewer 5xxs.

Thanks Jonas — we just ran a controlled retry batch and error rate dropped to ~0.05%. Good to confirm the routing change helped.

Two asks before we close the loop:
1) Can Redwood add an explicit SLA escape hatch for partners when a kernel/patch rollout impacts their warm pool? Right now our SLOs are tight and we need a documented remediation path.
2) We’d like the runbook for how you’ll coordinate with us on future rollouts (pre-notify window, canary percentage, rollback criteria).

I attached the full error dump for your infra team to reference: catalyst-error-log-20260711.txt

Alex
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@catalystsys.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: partner-support@catalystsys.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: connector errors in production (Catalyst <-> Redwood)

Alex — thanks for the test and the detailed error dump. Glad the routing work bought us time.

From Partnerships & Ops perspective I propose the following (short-term + formalization):
- Short-term: add a partner escalation path in our support portal that routes to a dedicated partner on-call for any API/connector rollouts that impact production (we’ll update contact card and increase paging priority). Target: live within 72 hours.
- Formal SLA addendum: we can offer a rollback/escape clause tied to kernel/major runtime rollouts that affect a customer’s dedicated warm pool. Wording draft: "If a Redwood runtime rollout causes >0.5% increase in 5xxs for a partner over a 30-minute window, Redwood will invoke an emergency rollback or traffic re-route until stability is confirmed." We’ll surface legal language after signoff.
- Runbook: I attached a proposed runbook PDF (integration-runbook-proposed.pdf) that documents pre-rollout notice (48h for planned major kernel upgrades), canary split (2–5%), rollback criteria, and partner communication cadence. Please review and call out items you need tightened.

Operationally — Mateo will coordinate timelines with Catalyst and I’ll shepherd the SLA addendum through Legal. Jonas, please add a short verification checklist to RED-3245 so infra can act quickly if we need a rollback.

Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
